almond_milk: Read the Nutrition Facts for added sugars, then calcium and vitamin D.
applesauce: Read the ingredient list; it should stop after one word.
bacon: Find the pasture seal on the bacon pack.
bagels: Check the ingredients for ascorbic acid; ask about the water bath.
baking_powder: Read the tin for an explicit no-aluminum claim.
baking_soda_soak: Soak the fruit twelve minutes, then rinse it clean.
bbq_sauce_marinades: Read the first three ingredients for corn syrup and smoke.
beans_dried_vs_canned: Read dry bags for beans alone; check tins for a BPA-free claim.
beef_cuts_basics: Check the tray’s seal and the AGA and USDA marks.
beef_grassfed_vs_grainfed: Find the AGA seal and 100% grass-fed wording.
beef_veal: Read the label for pasture rearing and a humane seal.
berries_picking: Flip the container and check for juice stains or fuzz.
bison: Read the pack for bison alone and the AGA mark beside the cut.
bottled_water_buying: Read the water source on the label; look for spring.
bread_aisle: Read the first ingredient for “whole”, then check which stamp is shown.
breakfast_cereal: Compare the added-sugars line and check which Whole Grain Stamp is shown.
broth: Read the list for named bones and vegetables, then sodium on the panel.
bulk_bins_buying: Choose the full, busy bins over a dusty half-empty one.
buns_rolls: Read the name on the bag for “whole wheat”, not “wheat” or “enriched”.
butcher_counter_asking: Ask what came in today and when it was cut.
canned_coconut_milk: Check the can’s lining claim for BPA-free alongside a two-ingredient list.
canned_fish_choosing: Read the species name and check for fish, water or olive oil.
canned_soup: Read the front for “low sodium” versus “reduced sodium”; they differ.
canned_tuna: Read the catch wording for pole, troll, FAD-free or school methods.
cheese_real_vs_processed: Read the printed name; skip cheese followed by food or product.
chicken_breast: Find the Certified Humane Pasture Raised seal alongside USDA certification.
chicken_cuts_basics: Check for cream-yellow skin and an AWA seal on the bird.
clams_mussels_oysters: Tap to check that each shell shuts, then find the bag’s harvest tag.
cocoa: Read the label for “processed with alkali” after the name.
coconut_milk_beverage: Read the carton for “beverage” in the name, then the thickeners.
coconut_water: Read the ingredient line; skip aseptic boxes and added sugar.
coffee_beans: Check the bag’s seal and keep the coffee closed between uses.
condiments: Skip jars naming soybean or canola as the first oil.
cooking_oils: Check the bottle names one oil, without a blend.
cornmeal_polenta_grits: Find the USDA seal; skip degerminated on the grain bag.
cottage_cheese: Read for milk and cream first; skip thickening gums.
crab: Watch for leg movement before picking a live crab.
crackers: Read for white flour, hydrogenated oil or soy flour; skip any listed.
cream_cheese: Read the list for cream, milk, salt and cultures.
cream_vs_creamer: Read the panel for milkfat percent — real cream states 36% or 10.5%.
cured_pork: Read the ingredients for pork and salt alone.
dairy_case: Read the side panel for added vitamins, then any grazing or filtering claim.
dark_chocolate: Read the cocoa percentage, then count the ingredients on the back.
deli: Check the cold case first; meats, cheeses and salads all need it.
deli_liverwurst_pate: Read the ingredients: liver first, animal fat, no binders or extenders.
deli_meat_uncured: Ask for fresh slices from a whole roast bearing an Uncured label.
deli_salads: Check the date; keep it at the back of the fridge, not the door.
dried_fruit: Read the ingredients for sulfites or sugar added to the fruit.
dried_herbs: Read for one herb; skip blends listing citric acid or MSG.
egg_duck_quail: Read the carton for duck and pastured wording.
egg_labels: Find USDA Organic on the carton beside the other seal.
farmed_fish_by_species: Find the ASC logo on the fish pack.
fermented: Check the label for “raw” or “unpasteurized”, then the list for vinegar.
fermented_pickles: Read the ingredients for vinegar; none listed means a fermented pickle.
flour_basics: Read the bag for whole wheat before choosing flour.
freezing_produce: Blanch vegetables sixty seconds, chill them, then freeze flat.
fresh_pasta: Check the date, and use an opened pack within 2 to 3 days.
frozen: Check for grayish-brown or white dried patches; that is freezer burn.
frozen_fries: Read the ingredient list for potatoes and the oil used before freezing.
frozen_meals: Check the inspection mark, then follow the package directions to heat it.
frozen_nuggets: Check for “natural proportions”, which means 50 to 65 percent light meat.
frozen_pizza: Check a crust sold as whole wheat for whole wheat flour throughout.
frozen_vs_fresh_produce: Read the bag’s ingredient list for one word: the vegetable.
frozen_waffles: Read the list for “wheat flour”, which is not a whole grain flour.
ghee: Check the jar lists one dairy fat, without oil blended in.
gluten_free_bread: Read the flours in ingredient order; skip unless the first is marked whole.
goat_sheep_dairy: Read the ingredients for which animal’s milk went in.
grains_beyond_rice: Check the grain bag for a single ingredient and an organic seal.
grassfed_butter: Read for cream and salt; skip any natural flavor entry.
ground_beef_lean_ratio: Find the lean ratio beside the AGA seal on the pack.
ground_turkey: Read for thigh and breast meat alone, then check the certification seal.
ham: Read the product name’s opening word for Uncured, then check for pork and salt.
honey_adulteration: Look through the jar for cloudiness from pollen, rather than clear honey.
hot_dogs: Find the AGA seal, then count the ingredients.
hot_soy_sauce: Read the ingredients for wheat, and the front for “gluten-free”.
hummus: Read the ingredients for canola or soybean oil; skip either.
ice_cream: Read for cream, milk, yolks and real vanilla; skip flavor words or extenders.
jam: Read the label for “reduced sugar”, then keep the opened jar cold.
judging_meat_at_the_case: Check the package is sealed and not leaking juices, then smell it.
ketchup_mustard: Read the list for tomatoes, vinegar and spices.
kimchi: Check the packed date, then read the list for fish sauce or shrimp.
kombucha: Check the glass bottle for organic wording and black tea in the ingredients.
label_artificial_color: Check candy, frosting and white dressings for “color added” near the list’s end.
label_cage_free: Skip cartons claiming cage-free without a seal for outdoor access.
label_cold_pressed_expeller: Read the bottle’s pressing method: cold or expeller.
label_front_vs_back: Read three things: ingredient list, added sugars, serving size.
label_grass_fed_term: Look for “100%” or “grass-finished” printed on the package.
label_ingredient_order: Stop reading at “contains 2% or less” — the rest is a trace.
label_lightly_sweetened: Scan the ingredient list for syrup, cane juice, and concentrate.
label_made_with_real: Count how far down it sits. Past third is a trace.
label_multigrain_vs_whole_grain: Read for 100% whole grain, or whole before the grain name.
label_natural: Look for a defined word instead: organic, grass-finished, or pasture-raised.
label_no_added_hormones: Look for a third-party verifier on the beef and dairy claim.
label_no_artificial_flavors: Look for “natural flavors” further down the list — the claim leaves it in.
label_nonGMO_vs_organic: Buy the USDA Organic seal alone — paying for both is paying twice.
label_organic_scope: Flip the organic box over. The seal says nothing about the ingredients.
label_pasture_raised_feed: Check both claims for seals: AWA Pasture Raised plus USDA Organic.
label_serving_size: Check both packages list the same serving size before comparing anything.
label_sugar_free_substitutes: Read the list for erythritol, maltitol, stevia, sucralose — one is there.
label_third_party_seals: Trace the seal to an organization, not the brand’s own logo.
label_wild_vs_farm_raised: Read the tag for wild or farm-raised, plus origin and catch details.
lamb_goat: Look for pale pink fat on chops carrying the AWA pasture stamp.
lard_tallow: Read for a single fat and pastured wording on the label.
lobster: Check claw movement; choose frozen tails that feel hard without ice glaze.
maple_syrup: Read for pure maple syrup alone; skip corn syrup in the ingredients.
mayo: Read the ingredients for which oil comes first, whatever the front says.
mercury_by_fish: Check the species name on the can for sardines.
miso: Read the ingredients for which grain went in with the soybeans.
molasses_whole_cane_sweeteners: Read the list for one ingredient: molasses or dehydrated cane juice.
muesli: Read the ingredients for sugar, honey or syrup beyond the dried fruit.
natto: Check the date on the pack, since chilled natto keeps only days.
nut_butter_ingredients: Read the list for nuts and salt; skip sugar, palm or hydrogenated oils.
nutritional_yeast: Read the ingredients for added vitamins, which mark a fortified yeast.
nuts_raw_vs_roasted: Find raw on the sealed pack; skip sugared or coated nuts.
oat_milk: Read the ingredients for added vitamins and minerals, then the stabilizers.
oats_steelcut_rolled_instant: Skip instant packets listing flavor or sugar; read for whole grain oats.
olive_oil_grades: Choose a dark bottle or metal tin; skip clear plastic.
olives: Check the jar date, and finish an opened jar within 2 weeks.
organ_meats: Check liver or heart packs for an AGA or organic seal.
organic_worth_it_by_type: Spend the organic money on berries, greens, and apples.
pasta_dry: Turn the box over and read the flour and any added ingredients.
pasta_sauce: Check that tomatoes lead, with oil named and no sugar or natural flavors.
pastries_muffins: Read the fat in the ingredients, or ask the baker if it is butter.
pesto: Read the oil on the list; olive oil should be the only one.
pick_juice: Read the ingredient list for Red 40, Yellow 5, Yellow 6 or Blue 1.
plain_kefir: Read the kefir ingredients for milk and cultures alone.
plant_butter: Skip spreads listing palm, canola or a vegetable oil blend.
popcorn: Read the ingredients for anything listed besides popcorn.
pork_cuts_and_enhanced: Find an AWA or Certified Humane pasture seal on the chop pack.
potato_chips: Read the label for “made from dried potatoes”, the mark of a pressed chip.
poultry_chicken_wings: Check that the skin has no tears, then read the raising claims.
poultry_duck: Pick a whole bird with skin on and an AWA seal.
precut_produce_tradeoffs: Check the use-by date, since pre-cut spoils days before whole produce does.
prepared_meals: Check the case thermometer, and pans filled no higher than the rim.
pretzels: Read the first ingredient; skip refined white flour.
produce_apples_pears: Turn each apple or pear over and leave any bruised or damaged one behind.
produce_avocados: Check the skin for large indentations before choosing an avocado.
produce_bananas: Look for a little green at both the stem and tip.
produce_brassicas: Check for closed, dark green florets, then press the head for soft spots.
produce_citrus: Choose citrus that feels firm with unblemished rind, and leave the soft ones.
produce_grapes: Pick grapes held firmly on green stems; skip brown stems.
produce_green_beans: Rub a finger along the pod; skip lumpy sections.
produce_leafy_greens: Check the leaves stand crisp and fully green, then keep them cold at home.
produce_melons: Turn the melon over and check the rind for bruises or cuts.
produce_mushrooms: Look under the cap for pink or light tan gills.
produce_onions_garlic: Squeeze the bulb, smell it, and keep it out of the plastic bag.
produce_peppers: Choose thick-walled, firm peppers with bright color and a fresh green stem.
produce_potatoes: Read the bag or sign for the growing method before bagging.
produce_ripeness_by_item: Smell the stem end on anything that ripens after picking.
produce_root_vegetables: Press each root for firmness, and twist the tops off carrots before storing.
produce_seasonality: Read the farmers’ market as the signal for what is in season locally.
produce_stone_fruit: Look the fruit over for bruises or damage and skip any that shows one.
produce_storage: Keep apples and bananas out of the drawer with your greens and berries.
produce_tomatoes: Check the skin for blotchy green or brown patches; skip those tomatoes.
produce_tropical_fruit: Pick whole fruit with no bruises, then ripen on the counter.
rancidity_check: Skip clear bottles; check for a paint-and-crayon smell when opening oil.
raw_aged_cheese: Read the rind label for an age in months.
raw_cider_vinegar: Check the bottle’s bottom for cloudy strands of mother.
raw_kefir: Buy it from the refrigerated case, never the shelf-stable carton.
raw_milk: Buy from a farm you can visit that posts its test results.
revive_greens: Trim the stem ends and stand them in ice water thirty minutes.
rice_arsenic: Check the origin on the bag; skip brown rice syrup.
rice_cakes_puffed_grains: Skip flavor-coated grains or packs listing natural flavor or syrup.
rotisserie_chicken: Read the ingredient list for added starches or sweeteners.
salad_dressing: Read the oil on the list first, then count the ingredients.
salmon_wild_vs_farmed: Read for wild Alaskan, then check the flesh for a deep red color.
salsa: Read the ingredients for the acid: vinegar, lime or lemon juice.
salt: Look for gray, pink, red or beige crystals; skip iodized on the label.
sandwich_bread: Read the list’s top; skip enriched wheat flour, sugar or soybean oil.
sauerkraut: Read the ingredients for cabbage and salt only, with no vinegar listed.
scallops: Check the tray for milky pooling; look for dry-packed on the label.
seafood_certifications: Check the MSC program name, blue fish symbol and tracking code.
seafood_counter: Check the counter for clear eyes, ice and a species sign.
seafood_fish_roe: Read the jar for salmon roe and salt alone.
seafood_fresh_sardines_mackerel: Check these fish for bright stripes or shiny skin.
seafood_trout: Ask the counter whether the trout is wild, or farmed in the US.
seaweed: Read the sea vegetable’s name and country; skip packs from China.
seeds: Check the raw seed pack’s date and single-ingredient list.
shrimp_imported_vs_domestic: Read the bag for Gulf or US wild origin; check for shells.
smoked_salmon: Check the cold case, then read the label for origin and wild wording.
snack_bars: Read ingredients for brown rice syrup or agave; skip bars listing either.
snacks: Read for potatoes or corn, olive or coconut oil, and salt alone.
sour_cream: Skip tubs listing starch, gums or flavor words beside cream and cultures.
sourdough: Find a starter or culture in the bread’s ingredient list.
soy_milk: Read the ingredients for soybeans and water, then calcium and vitamin D if added.
specialty_flours: Count the types of flour listed; choose one with organic on the bag.
split_peas: Grab a sealed bag of dried peas or lentils and soak them overnight.
sprouted_grain_bread: Read for sprouted before each grain; skip loaves listing flour first.
sprouted_grains: Check the label names the grain as whole, not only its process.
sprouts_raw: Skip tubs with dry or slimy sprouts.
sugars: Read for dehydrated cane juice, beyond sugar alone.
tea: Read the ingredient list for tea leaves and nothing else.
tempeh: Read the ingredients for soybeans alone or added grains, and check for mold.
tortilla_chips: Read the ingredients for masa; plain cornmeal makes a corn chip instead.
tortillas: Check for masa or masa harina, then read for added wheat and fat.
trail_mix: Skip mixes listing sugar, chocolate or vegetable oil beside the nuts.
turkey_bacon: Read the name for Uncured, then check which meat leads the ingredient list.
turkey_whole: Read the tag for not basted and Certified Humane Pasture Raised.
venison_game: Ask whether each animal was handled separately and kept cold throughout.
vinegar: Read for apple cider, wine or balsamic on the label.
washing_produce: Scrub the firm ones with a brush. Rinse and spin the greens.
white_fish: Turn the fillet to check its gray-brown skin, then read the cod tag.
whole_spices: Pick intact seeds or sticks, rather than a ground blend.
whole_vs_reduced_fat_milk: Read beside the date; skip ultra-pasteurized and check the fat wording.
wild_rice: Read for wild rice alone, without white rice blended in.
yogurt_plain_vs_flavored: Read for milk and culture names; skip sugar, pectin or flavors.
